outcome: Since 26 January 2024, the general Virasoro conjecture (for all smooth projective varieties, all genera) remains open, but several further special/restricted cases have been proved by human mathematicians using traditional methods: the genus-0 and genus-1 parts of a generalized Virasoro conjecture for semisimple CohFTs (Guo–Zhang, arXiv:2502.18895, Feb 2025), a proof of the genus-1 Virasoro conjecture on the ambient state space of smooth Fano complete intersections (Guo–Zhang–Zhou, arXiv:2608.29870, Aug 2026), and a proof of Virasoro constraints for the relative Gromov-Witten theory of all smooth projective effective orbifold curves, from which the absolute Jiang-Tseng Virasoro conjecture follows for such curves (Hu–Jin–Ke–Lu–Tseng–Wu, arXiv:2609.01300, Sep 2026). A related paper connecting the Virasoro conjecture to the λg-conjecture (Xin Wang, arXiv:2412.05287, Nov 2024) also proves the λg-conjecture in new cases assuming/using Virasoro-conjecture machinery, but is a related/derived result rather than a case of the Virasoro conjecture itself.
summary: The Virasoro conjecture as stated (a certain generating function encoding the Gromov-Witten invariants of a smooth projective variety is fixed by an action of half the Virasoro algebra) remains open in general — it is known for genus 0 (Liu-Tian, 1998), for semisimple CohFTs and some toric/flag/Grassmannian/curve cases from before the frozen date, and (per the article) in all genera only for a point and Calabi-Yau 3-folds. Since 26 January 2024 several further cases have been settled by traditional (non-AI) mathematics: (1) Guo-Zhang (arXiv:2502.18895, Feb 2025) prove ancestor and generalized Virasoro conjectures for semisimple CohFTs in full and verify the genus-0 part more generally; (2) Guo-Zhang-Zhou (arXiv:2608.29870, Aug 2026) prove the genus-1 Virasoro conjecture on the ambient state space of Fano complete intersections via wall-crossing and quantum Lefschetz methods; (3) Hu-Jin-Ke-Lu-Tseng-Wu (arXiv:2609.01300, Sep 2026) prove Virasoro constraints for relative Gromov-Witten theory of all smooth projective effective orbifold curves, yielding the absolute Jiang-Tseng Virasoro conjecture for such curves as a corollary. Each of these is a genuine case of the stated problem (a restriction to a class of varieties/genus), not a variant, so status is 'partial' with resolution_direction 'confirmed' (the settled cases go the way the conjecture predicts; no counterexample). I read all three papers via fetches of their arXiv abstract pages; none mentions any AI system, language model, or machine-learning tool anywhere — these are traditional human-proved results in algebraic geometry using wall-crossing formulas, quantum Lefschetz theory, and CohFT/Frobenius-manifold techniques. I also searched broadly for any AI/LLM connection to the Virasoro conjecture or nearby Gromov-Witten work (including AlphaProof/AlphaEvolve-style automated theorem proving) and found nothing relevant; one superficially matching hit, arXiv:2510.21741 'Virasoro algebra and Sugawara constructions formally in Lean' (Kytölä, Oct 2025), is an unrelated Lean formalization of the Virasoro algebra's representation theory in a different (non-Gromov-Witten) context, not a formalization of this conjecture, and its page gave no information about AI tool use in any case. I did not find a paper claiming the full/general Virasoro conjecture was proved or disproved in the window. The triage's two 'found' items check out as real, on-topic, human-authored partial results; I found one additional in-window partial result (arXiv:2502.18895) the triage did not surface, and one related-but-distinct result (arXiv:2412.05287, connecting Virasoro to the λg-conjecture) that I judged a related problem rather than a direct case, discussed in summary rather than counted toward status.
competing_reading: One could argue the Xin Wang λg-conjecture paper (arXiv:2412.05287, Nov 2024) should also count as 'partial' progress on the Virasoro conjecture itself, since it proves the λg-conjecture unconditionally in genus 0 and 1 and ties it to Virasoro constraints; I read it as a related/derived conjecture (the λg-conjecture, a distinct statement about Hodge integrals) rather than a restriction of the Virasoro conjecture's own generating-function statement, so I did not use it as the status-defining event. If a reader defines 'the problem' more broadly to include consequences for closely tied conjectures, this event could be pulled earlier (Nov 2024) without changing ai_role or resolution_direction.
what_would_settle_it: A closer reading of arXiv:2412.05287's proof to see whether it establishes new instances of the Virasoro conjecture itself (rather than only using Virasoro as a hypothesis/tool for the λg-conjecture) would settle whether it belongs in status_sources.
